chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Halbi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the expiation for an oath, he should feed ten poor people; for each poor person, a mud of wheat or a mud of flour and a handful, or their clothing, for each person two garments, or freeing a slave. He has the choice among these three; whichever of the three he does. If he is unable to do any one of the three, then fasting is upon him for three days.

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What are the options for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the hierarchical expiation for breaking an oath, prioritizing material charity (feeding or clothing ten poor people) or manumission, with fasting as a tertiary fallback. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, emphasizing accessibility by allowing the least burdensome option that the individual can afford, thereby ensuring the expiation is achievable for all socioeconomic classes.
